majors.issue: The in-flight excuse checks only r.sent.Before(m.returned). It ignores which release was current when the request was sent. Mark i bans r00..r(i-1), but r(i-1) is the only release a request in flight across switch i may legitimately get. Mark i-1's ban window ends at marks[i].called, measured by arrival. So a response to a request sent after switch i-1 returned that arrives after switch i was called, and carries a release older than r(i-1), is checked by no mark. The spec criterion 'no request sent after the switch returned is answered with an older release id' is therefore not proven for mark i-1. Before the repair, the cumulative ban list of mark i caught it.
majors.scenario: A request is written 10 ms after the r04 switch returns. A stale route sends it to r00, which retention keeps as a retired release within its drain. It answers after 3 s, during r05's Deploy health gate or just after SwitchRelease(r05) was called, and after the first r05 answer. Mark 4 skips it because it arrived after marks[5].called. Mark 5 excuses it because sent < marks[5].returned. TestTenDeploysUnderLoadDropNothing passes although a request sent after the r04 switch was answered by r00. Fix: excuse only an answer whose release was current when its request was sent (for mark i, the previous mark's release, or r00 for the first; r10 for the rollback mark).

minors.issue: Carried from round 2: startLoad's generator is stopped only on the success path. A t.Fatalf in tenDeploys, deploy or switchTo skips l.stop(), so the ticker goroutine keeps sending requests until the test process exits.
minors.scenario: Deploy(r04) fails in TestTenDeploysUnderLoadDropNothing: the proxy is stopped, but the load goroutine keeps dialling the closed port 50 times a second while TestRollbackUnderLoadIsUnderFiveSeconds runs in parallel. This costs CPU and adds noise; no assertion is affected.
